A1.justification: Both PDFs contain readable main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices describing the same research. Despite the AMoE-to-SigLino renaming and expanded model family, retained methods and experiments can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, retrieval, segmentation, and grounding experiments, alongside distillation, data-curation, positional-encoding, and expert-specialization analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds model-variant evaluations, single-teacher grounding controls, and qualitative grounding-adaptation results.

M1.justification: v2 expands the proposed architecture family with a 0.6B dense student replacing MoE layers with standard FFNs and a sparse top-2-of-28 MoE, alongside the retained top-6 model. The core distillation recipe remains unchanged. The expanded grounding section documents an approach already used in v1 rather than establishing a newly introduced grounding method.

E1.justification: Training-data sources, classification and retrieval benchmarks, semantic segmentation, RefCOCO/+/g grounding, and unseen-resolution testing are retained. Additional model variants and teacher controls use existing dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds TIPS comparisons for classification and segmentation and introduces SigLIP2-only and DINOv3-only initialization controls for grounding, substantially extending the alternatives tested. RADIOv2.5-L classification rows are removed from Table 1, although that comparator remains in segmentation and retrieval.

E3.justification: The experimental design expands to dense, sparse, 30M, and 70M students and single-teacher grounding controls. Additionally, v1 specifies 100k ImageNet reference images for kNN generally, whereas v2 restricts that statement to ablations without specifying the main comparison's reference-set size. The retained main MoE training schedule is unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds single-versus-multiple-teacher grounding analysis (Table 6), architecture and parameter-budget comparisons, and PCA evidence examining Gram anchoring during grounding adaptation (Figure 3). Existing numerical Gram-anchoring, ARKD, curation, PHI-S, and RoPE analyses remain. The CKA analysis moves from the main text to supplementary Section 10.

E5.justification: Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seed disclosures, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures. Additional result rows retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice, and the training-dynamics plots are unchanged.

E6.justification: v2 adds results for four model variants and teacher-only grounding controls. For the retained MoE, Table 2 changes Cityscapes/ADE20k/PASCAL-VOC scores from 64.89/51.37/84.40 to 64.36/52.23/87.05; RADIOv2.5-H scores also change. Table 1 revises ImageNet kNN values alongside changed protocol wording, so these are not established same-setting gains. Original retrieval and numerical ablation results are largely retained.

T1.justification: Section 3.5 adds an explicit definition of normalized patch Gram matrices and the anchoring objective (Equation 8). The supplementary RoPE discussion removes the explicit aspect-ratio coordinate mapping. Core distillation and ARKD mathematics remain unchanged, while the existing CKA formulation is relocated; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract broadens the contribution from an MoE model to a dense-and-MoE family with five checkpoints. The principal claims about ARKD, token-balanced batching, and curated data remain. Grounding transfer receives greater abstract and conclusion emphasis, but was already claimed and evaluated in v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds a mechanism hypothesis connecting grounding adaptation to patch features aligning with the CLS token, and interprets Gram anchoring as preserving inter-patch geometry. It also interprets the new architecture comparisons as an efficiency-performance trade-off. Existing ARKD, PHI-S, and expert-specialization interpretations are largely retained.

D1.justification: v2 documents grounding heads, Dice/Focal and text objectives, and dense/sparse configurations. Conversely, it omits v1's segmentation-probe epochs, batch size and learning rate, grounding distillation's 42k-step budget and hidden dimension, explicit RoPE coordinates, and fuller ensembling specification. The promised supplementary ensembling details are absent. Core optimizer, hardware, and pseudocode disclosures remain.

R1.justification: Related work expands substantially with Grounding VLM and Early-Fusion VLM discussions, positioning the approach against modular architectures and connecting it to works including Florence-2, Pixel-LLM, Chameleon, and MoMa. TIPS and other references are added, while the Xiong positional-encoding reference is removed.

P1.justification: Beyond renaming, v2 revises the abstract and experimental narrative, adds a grounding method section, expands related work, and relocates CKA analysis to the appendix. Ensembling and ablation explanations are shortened, and the supplement is reorganized. The small-model discussion is duplicated in supplementary Sections 6 and 14.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn to include the grounding architecture, Figure 3 adds adaptation PCA comparisons, four result tables are added, and main comparison tables gain model rows. The CKA figure and benchmark-specific curation table move to the appendix. Most existing supplementary visualizations are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 adds valuable architecture and teacher-complementarity comparisons and clarifies grounding adaptation. However, new Table 1 kNN averages do not match the displayed scores: the dense model reports 90.70 although its five entries average 88.90, and the sparse model reports 89.80 versus 87.84. Several reproducibility details also disappear. These issues affect central comparisons and reproducibility, leaving the net quality direction uncertain despite the useful additions.
